runbook_name: SHS Operator Runbook V1 - Phase 7: ClientOps
goal: Document how SHS manages a launched client after delivery.
entry_condition: Phase 6 Launch is ClientOps Active, final approval, launch date, client signoff, support tier, handoff notes, version record, and ClientOps record are available, ClientOps owner/support owner is assigned, open maintenance or post-launch watch items are transferred, and public/report claims remain behind required gates.
exit_condition: Client actively managed: client record, maintenance board, support tickets, system health, version history, upgrade opportunities, monthly review cadence, handoff file, owner assignment, and governance boundaries are active.

surfaces.purpose: Active ClientOps records, maintenance board, support tickets, system health, version history, upgrade opportunities, monthly review, and exports.
Local ClientOps records and operational data model.
Project snapshot, monthly review, maintenance, support ticket, system health, and upgrade opportunity exports.
Pre-launch and launch handoff context before ClientOps takes over.
Trust-aware reporting/readiness context for report candidate material.
Truth/readiness/public approval authority for claims and public-facing facts.
Links SHF-Next /ops/clientops to SHRV1 Agent Fabric and Reports governance surfaces.
Classifies /ops/clientops as internal ClientOps for shs_admin and shs_clientops.

operator_checklist: Confirm Phase 6 exit status is ClientOps Active.
Open or create the active ClientOps record.
Confirm client identity, business identity, project ID, package, support tier, active modules, routes, reports, and owner.
Attach or confirm the handoff file.
Transfer launch version record into version history.
Create or update maintenance board items.
Triage open support tickets and assign owner, priority, status, and next action.
Record current system health and next health check date.
Track upgrade opportunities, renewal timing, and expansion candidates.
Establish monthly review cadence and next review date.
Confirm reports use trust-aware Reports and Truth Spine readiness when report/public claims are in scope.
Keep ClientOps private operational records out of public SHF surfaces.
Treat ClientOps exports as local ClientOps artifacts unless governed intake is explicitly approved.
Mark the client actively managed only when ClientOps record, maintenance, support, health, version, upgrade, review, and handoff file are current.

client_record: Renewal or upgrade timing if known.
support_tickets: Response expectation based on support tier.
system_health: Broken routes or errors if found.
Report/public claim readiness if in scope.
version_history: Rollback or recovery note if applicable.
upgrade_opportunities: Source: client request, operator observation, monthly review, support trend, or system health issue.
handoff_file: Client contacts and escalation path where appropriate.

governance_boundary.clientops_role: ClientOps feeds SHS operational truth by default. Raw ClientOps records remain in SHS unless downstream governance explicitly allows transfer.
blocked_actions: Direct SHF Impact Data Spine mutation.
Publishing ClientOps reports without required trust/readiness gates.
Exposing ClientOps private operational records on public routes.
allowed_governed_path: SHF Impact Data Spine only after approval

definition_of_done: Version history includes launch baseline and post-launch changes.
Handoff file is complete and private-safe.
Report/public impact candidates remain behind governance gates.
findings: The ClientOps governance audit identifies /ops/clientops in SHF-Next as the active ClientOps surface.

ClientOps functional areas include active records, maintenance board, support tickets, system health, version history, upgrade opportunities, monthly review, SHS monthly report preview/export, and multiple operational exports.
ClientOps is internal/private and not public SHF impact data.
SHRV1 admin ops routes are protected under admin routing, while SHF-Next /ops/clientops is classified as internal ClientOps with shs_admin and shs_clientops roles.
ClientOps exports remain local ClientOps artifacts unless governed intake occurs.
Reports and Watchtower expose governance context without making ClientOps public.
launch_blockers: Production auth is still outside this runbook phase.
ClientOps currently depends on consumer-app local/internal workflow context rather than SHRV1 durable ClientOps backend persistence.
No dedicated ClientOps formal V1 governance check exists unless ClientOps becomes an official governance-enforced layer rather than an ops surface.
Real ClientOps-to-governance intake is not implemented and should only be added at approved boundaries.
Visible ClientOps governance banner in SHF-Next remains a future owner-approved consumer-app change.
post_v1_improvements: Add durable ClientOps persistence when owner approves runtime work.
Add structured ClientOps monthly review model.
Add support ticket and maintenance board exports with governance labels.
Add visible internal-only ClientOps governance banner in SHF-Next.
Add Source Registry intake mapping for ClientOps exports when real governed intake is implemented.
Add automated checks that prevent ClientOps records from appearing on public routes.

npm run build.notes: Build passed with the existing Vite large-chunk warning.

npm run check:governance.notes: Master registry, proposal, Truth Spine, Oracle, AI Guardrails, Game Theory, data/governance layers, and duplicate cleanup checks passed.
